_note: STAGE 1-2 PLACEHOLDER DATA. Synthetic waveforms + sample teaching text to test layout only. Real PTB-XL records and Mark's clinical text replace these at stage 5.

rois.R: Rate around 75 per minute and regular. The R-R intervals march out evenly across the strip.
rois.O: A P wave sits before every QRS, and every QRS follows a P. Upright P waves in the inferior leads — this is sinus.
rois.I: PR interval sits within normal limits. The QRS is narrow, under three small squares. QT looks proportionate to the rate.
rois.S: Baseline ST segments across all territories. No elevation, no depression, T waves upright where expected.

rois.O: P wave before each QRS — the underlying rhythm is sinus. Don't stop here: the rhythm being ordinary is exactly when the ST segment matters most.
rois.I: PR within normal limits. QRS narrow.
rois.S: ST elevation in the inferior leads — II, III and aVF (the orange group). Glance across at I and aVL for any reciprocal change. Territory only — this tool names where, not what to do about it.

rois.O: P waves are present before the QRS complexes.
rois.I: The QRS is broad — wider than three small squares. That widening is the finding to notice at this step.
rois.S: Look at the ST segments and T waves in the context of the wide QRS. Describe what you see by territory.
